 Oral Judgment
(Per: Hon'Ble Mrs Justice K.S.Mudagal)

Under the above application, the appellants are
seeking condonation of delay of 800 days in filing the appeal.

The application is seriously opposed
by the respon
dent .

The explanation in the affidavit filed in support of the application is that the appellants have no knowledge about Court NC: 2024:KHC:37356-DB proceedings, only on the advice of their counsel, they have filed this appeal.
2. It is material to note that challenging the very award, the insurer has preferred the connected appeal in the year 2018 itself.

In that appeal, the present appellants were served and appeared through their counsel on 04.09.2018, but this appeal is filed after four years of their appearance of their counsel in the connected matter.
So far as alleged ignorance of the appellants, the defendant himself has signed in his affidavit in English.
Moreover, he had appointed an advocate in the connected case in 2018 itself.
3. The condonation of delay is not a mere formality.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pathupati Subba Reddy (Died) by L.Rs. & Ors. v. The Special Deputy Collector reported in 2024 SCC OnLine 513, has held that the law of limitation is founded on the public policy.

The public policy Smt.Lavanya vs Afsar Khan on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137849565/
2 requires that there should be an end to the litigation and the parties cannot litigate in eternity on vicious grounds.
In the light of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, we are not inclined to exercise discretion to condone the delay.
I.A.No.1/2022 and consequently, the appeal are dismissed.
